title: Publish an Agent OS auth-boundary architecture skill
description: Create a reusable, site-facing skill that explains the auth and execution boundary across NotMe, Signet, Interlace/Cloister, LLO, Rosary, and Mache. It must distinguish identity issuance, evidence and signature verification, capability/grant translation, local request binding, backend confinement, and receipt/audit responsibilities. Explicitly state what LLO must not reimplement: NotMe and Signet trust roots, Interlace workload identity, or product policy. Include one end-to-end flow and a responsibility matrix, and link to the LLO execution/v1 and conformance follow-on beads.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in skill or document is published from 0day-api, with a responsibility matrix and end-to-end flow reviewed against NotMe, Signet, Interlace/Cloister, and LLO contracts; no component is described as re-authenticating another component trust domain.

title: Published 0.1.0 was already behind 0day within hours — port the contract changes and release 0.2.0
description:
Two contract changes landed in 0day AFTER the extraction and were missing from the published package:

1. One coupling vocabulary. EDGE_KINDS (names plus descriptions) lived in derive.ts while EDGE_KIND_VALUES (the enum) lived in the contract, with nothing keeping them equal. Now a single declaration with the enum derived from its keys, so adding a name without a description is not expressible.

2. The cross-reference refinement on SiteMap: every kind used must be described in edge_kinds, and every resolved_by must name a key in resolution. Neither is expressible in JSON Schema, nor in capnp, which is why this layer stays hand-written when the contract is re-rooted.

The second matters more for a package than it did for 0day. Inside 0day, resolved_by to resolution was enforced indirectly by re-deriving and diffing against a committed artifact. A consumer running their own extractors has no committed artifact to diff against, so the guarantee did not exist for them at all.

0.2.0 rather than 0.1.1: this rejects documents that previously parsed, which under 0.x is a minor bump.

Verified in the BUILT dist rather than in source. Gate green, workerd 5/5, fidelity byte-identical at 52145 bytes.

Standing note: pnpm rewrites workspace:* to an EXACT version, so collect pins core exactly and every core release forces a collect release. Fine for two packages in lockstep, worth revisiting before it is six — workspace:^ emits a caret range instead.
acceptance_criteria: The built dist rejects an edge whose kind is absent from edge_kinds and whose resolved_by names no resolution rule; task check passes; versions are 0.2.0.

title: Port the unexamined-config detector from 0day, where it cannot survive the package swap
description:
The detector was written in 0day/tools/graph/lib/providers.ts on branch feat/0day-11da43-unexamined. That file is DELETED by the package swap (0day-a37536), so the branch could never merge — its content had to move here or be lost.

What it does: records root-level config files the collector saw and has no parser for, so a parser gap becomes a finding rather than silence. unresolved only covers declarations that were parsed and failed to resolve; a format with no parser is never attempted, so the coupling is absent rather than recorded, and absent is indistinguishable from there being nothing there.

The real case that prompted it: canonical-hours declares a coupling to vigil in a root .vigil.toml. It appears in no collection at all.

Membership is AUTHORED (UNPARSED_FORMATS), not pattern-matched. The first version used a regex for things that look like config, which reported .prettierrc.json with the same weight as .vigil.toml while still missing anything whose filename did not match. A guess dressed as a finding is worse than silence, because silence does not claim to have looked.

classify() is consulted first, so an entry disappears the moment a parser is added — the list shrinks as coverage grows rather than becoming a stale complaint.

Still only half the work: unexamined now rides in selectManifests output but does not reach the lock or the published artifact. Per the tracing done in 0day-11da43, notes[] — including the existing capped_dirs depth-cap gaps — go into a collect-time console report and are DISCARDED. So the existing coverage-gap machinery is invisible to consumers too, and the published claim rests entirely on unresolved. Finishing this means adding the field to the lock schema and the entity derived half, which needs a re-collect to populate.
acceptance_criteria: selectManifests returns unexamined, and a repo with a root .vigil.toml reports it while .prettierrc.json and parsed manifests do not.

title: Onboard rsry bead tracking + pre-commit framework
description: Set up .beads/ (SQLite store), AGENTS.md, and .pre-commit-config.yaml matching the convention shared across canonical-hours/cloister/rosary/mache: rsry's bead-export-sync hook, prettier auto-fix on commit, basic file hygiene, task ci as a pre-push gate.
acceptance_criteria: pre-commit run --all-files passes clean; rsry hooks status reports current hooks
